assessment: Large-cover rework and rounded-corner installation failures suggest different possible mismatches; their causes remain unestablished. Both combinations below are hypotheses requiring bounded trials.

openings.claim: Combine customer geometry confirmation with staged first-cover allowance calibration at the order-to-cutting-card interface.
openings.delta: Measurements alone cannot correct a faulty allowance; calibration on reference tables alone cannot detect customer corner geometry. Together they could calibrate construction against the intended installation before remaining panels are cut.
openings.prediction: The combination reduces first-placement failures more than either component alone, especially for large covers or tables differing from reference geometry.
openings.probe: Use six willing customers to record actual dimensions and corners. Compare four reversible offcut corner mockups: current practice, confirmed geometry only, calibrated allowance only, and both. Seat them against the measured target geometries; record mismatch and work time. Validate a first complete cover before releasing each affected cutting card, then record first-placement fit, design and total time for all 40.
assumptions: Customer measurements are sufficiently accurate and representative.
Trials and staged cutting fit the three-week window, existing machines, 350-unit budget and 8% area-waste ceiling.

openings.claim: Combine measured two-axis wash compensation with grain- and print-constrained nesting at the compensated-pattern-to-stock-layout interface.
openings.delta: Compensation could improve washed fit while consuming additional cloth; nesting could recover usable area without correcting shrinkage. Their interaction could accommodate necessary dimensional corrections within purchased stock.
openings.prediction: For stock exhibiting meaningful shrinkage, jointly planned compensated patterns retain washed fit while staying below 8% cutting waste by area; uncompensated layouts or compensation alone miss one of those outcomes.
openings.probe: Measure retained samples along both axes through the stipulated wash test. Compare compensated and current patterns under current and revised nesting, keeping visible design orientation fixed. Calculate area waste before cutting; verify a compensated sewn trial for fit, removability and wash survival.
assumptions: A feasible layout exists for required designs and sizes.
Measurement and nesting effort keep median total working time at or below 32 minutes.
